status: post_readback_generality test fixed before geography endpoint
question: Is species-specific same-SiteID chorus memory geographically repeatable across the NAAMP domain even though the magnitude of the rainfall effect varies among states?
source_model: Exactly the NAAMP_SPECIES_SPECIFIC_SITE_MEMORY_V0_1 pair x species fixed-effect model, including adjustment for other-species prior strong-chorus richness and prior site effort.

tests.leave_one_state_out: Refit after omitting each state in turn. PASS if all same-species-memory coefficients remain >0; strong PASS if all 95% CIs remain entirely >0.
tests.deterministic_route_split: Assign State:RouteNumber to A/B by first SHA256 byte (<128=A, otherwise B). Fit each fold independently. Both folds must have same-species-memory beta >0 with complete 95% CI >0.
tests.state_specific_description: Within states having >=100 informative pair x species groups, >=10 routes and >=10 species, report the same adjusted same-species-memory coefficient. No per-state success gate.

secondary: Repeat deterministic route split for wet_full (CallingIndex 3).
interpretation: If route-split and leave-one-state-out tests pass, the spatial reactivation rule is broadly repeatable within sampled NAAMP geography even if the rain-response magnitude itself is heterogeneous.
This is not evidence of global universality outside NAAMP.
No continuous occupancy, biological memory, individual fidelity, or causal rainfall effect is proven.
